decisions.reason: As a design-led decorative variant with only limited visible commitment beyond a standalone web page, this line likely involved modest incremental investment, so management can discontinue it relatively easily if it has not clearly proven itself.

This transparent burnout fabric sits close to the existing assortment and appears more like a collection extension than a strategic pillar, so escalation pressure to defend it is only moderate and a phase-out is fairly likely.

Because this burnout decorative fabric is another near-core style addition rather than a strongly publicized strategic move, the firm has limited need to justify keeping it if demand has been unexceptional.

A velour-like upholstery fabric builds on the firm’s established upholstery offer and customer-service model, so prior stocking, sampling, and sales effort create enough commitment for management to keep backing it absent clear failure evidence.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric fits functional customer needs and the firm’s dependable-supply positioning, making it easier for management to attribute any weak results to temporary market factors and continue with it.

This lining fabric is a practical adjacent product that can be supported through the existing warehouse and service system, so management is somewhat inclined to retain it rather than admit the launch was unnecessary.
